Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a large, well-defined mediastinal mass that is causing rightward deviation of the trachea and compression of the left main bronchus, resulting in left lower lobe atelectasis (evidenced by increased opacity and volume loss on the left). This presentation is most consistent with a neoplastic process such as a lymphoma or germ cell tumor rather than an infectious cyst or vascular malformation.
